citation: Architecture and Building Systems, ETH Zürich, City Energy Analyst, https://github.com/architecture-building-systems/CityEnergyAnalyst
description: City Energy Analyst (CEA) is an open-source urban building energy modelling platform that studies the effects, trade-offs and synergies of urban design scenarios and energy infrastructure plans at neighbourhood, district or city scale. It was created at ETH Zürich in 2013 and is hosted by the Chair of Architecture and Building Systems with uuen Company and a global community; the website says it has been used in over 75 countries, and version 3.11.0 was the current PyPI release on the day read. It collects building and street data for a selected area, simulates hourly demand for hundreds of buildings, estimates solar, geothermal and sewage heat potentials, designs heating and cooling networks, and compares supply options by cost, emissions and primary energy. Coverage: any area worldwide. Access: installers and source on GitHub, pip package, documentation and plug-ins. Licence: MIT; free. Caveats: automatic data collection relies on open sources whose building attributes may need local correction. Simulation uses: district energy and decarbonisation planning, including future climate scenarios. Related records: the Pirmasens CEA dataset, TEASER and the Modelblocks European building heat data.
